content: 1. Policy and Legislation on Noise: The status of these policies can be categorized as non-existent, passed but pending implementation, partially implemented, or fully implemented. This evaluation involves reviewing legislation, government reports, and discussions with relevant health authorities, such as occupational health divisions, industry regulators, and environmental departments. 2. Policy on Hearing Aid Provision: The development and implementation of policies or legislation for hearing aid provision are assessed every three years. The status is classified as non-existent, passed but pending implementation, partially implemented, or fully implemented. 3. Policy on Sign Language and Captioning Services: The development and implementation of policies or legislation for sign language and captioning services are reviewed every three years. 4. Guidelines for Monitoring Ototoxicity: The development and implementation of standard guidelines for monitoring ototoxicity are assessed every three years. These guidelines, issued by regulatory bodies or medical associations, are evaluated for their existence, partial implementation, or full implementation. Discussions with physicians, pediatricians, and specialists treating tuberculosis and AIDS are essential for this evaluation. 5. Strategic Plan Goals: The percentage of goals achieved in a five-year strategic plan for ear and hearing care (EHC) is reviewed annually. This involves calculating the number of goals accomplished during the year as a percentage of the total goals set for that year. 6. EHC Strategy Implementation: The percentage of districts, states, or counties implementing the EHC strategy is calculated as a proportion of the total number of such regions in the country. Similarly, the percentage of the population reached through the EHC strategy is determined based on the population covered by the strategy. 7. Infant Hearing Screening: The percentage of newborns screened through infant hearing screening programs is calculated annually. This is expressed as the number of infants screened as a percentage of the total number of births in the country during the same period. 8. School Hearing Screening: The percentage of schools implementing hearing screening programs as part of school health services is calculated annually. This is expressed as the number of schools conducting screenings as a percentage of the total number of schools in the country. 9. Tertiary-Level Health Facilities: The percentage of tertiary-level health facilities providing surgical (otological) and audiological services is reviewed every three years. This includes facilities such as medical colleges and referral hospitals. 10. Secondary-Level Health Facilities: The percentage of secondary-level health facilities offering surgical and audiological services is similarly reviewed every three years. These services include common otological surgeries and routine audiological assessments. 11. Primary-Level Health Facilities: The percentage of primary-level health facilities providing basic ear and hearing care services is assessed every three years. These services include diagnosing common ear conditions, managing ear diseases, and referring patients to higher-level facilities when necessary. 12. Age of Intervention for Hearing Loss: The average age of intervention for children with hearing loss identified through screening programs is calculated every three years. This data is obtained from hospitals running infant screening and early intervention programs. 13. Workforce Indicators: The availability of ENT specialists, audiological professionals, and other trained personnel is assessed every three years. Ratios are calculated per 100,000 population, with separate data for urban and rural areas. The number of ENT specialists and audiologists graduating annually is also monitored. 14. Training of Health Workers: The percentage of primary-level doctors and community-level health workers trained in EHC services is reviewed annually. This includes assessing whether training goals are met and the number of personnel trained. 15. Hearing Aid and Cochlear Implant Use: The number of people fitted with hearing aids and/or cochlear implants is calculated as a percentage of those with hearing loss or as a ratio per 100,000 population. This data is collected annually from government and NGO reports. 16. Maintenance and Follow-Up for Hearing Aid Users: The percentage of hearing aid users receiving regular maintenance and follow-up services is assessed annually. This indicates the effectiveness of follow-up services in ensuring the continued use of hearing aids. 17. Quality of Life Improvement: The percentage of hearing aid users reporting improved quality of life on follow-up is assessed through surveys conducted every ten years. This helps evaluate the impact of hearing care services on users' lives. 18. Immunization Coverage: The percentage of the target population receiving immunizations for rubella, meningitis, mumps, and measles is calculated annually. This data is obtained from government and WHO reports. 19. Cochlear Implant Recipients: The number of people receiving cochlear implants is calculated as a percentage of those with hearing loss or as a ratio per 100,000 population. This data is collected annually from government and distributor reports. These indicators provide a comprehensive framework for monitoring and evaluating ear and hearing care services, workforce development, and policy implementation at national and regional levels.
